claims: Mods are the release of 'function hooks' Boris Cherny teased early September; now a live feature

A mod can change what happens BEFORE an event, replace the event (INSTEAD), run AFTER, or WRAP both (e.g. for 'delete build folder': pause and list 41 files; move to Recycle Bin instead; show a receipt; back up first for undo)
Mods work in both the desktop app and the terminal
Prompt cache gives ~95% discount but goes cold after 1 hour; the cache-clock mod shows remaining time
Claude already knows how to generate and install mods; it creates a plugin, installs it, asks you to reload plugins; it then runs automatically like a hook
how_to_steps: Audit prompt: 'Audit how I use Claude Code. Read my last 30 sessions, see what I ask for over and over, then suggest 5 Claude Code mods that would fix these issues'
Pick one ('I like mod number one, implement that'); Claude writes the TypeScript plugin, installs it, asks to reload plugins
Turn off with natural language ('turn that mod off / remove it')

Diagram 'One event, up close: Claude deletes files' with columns 1 BEFORE (pause, list the 41 files, ask), 2 INSTEAD (move to Recycle Bin), 3 AFTER (receipt 'Deleted 41 files (2 MB) from build/'), 4 WRAP (back up first, Undo button); code snippets like 'const files = await listFiles(path)', 'await moveToTrash(path)'

Claude Code v2.1.287 terminal: 'Fable 5.1 with high effort - Claude Max', 'Get to finished work sooner with Opus 5.5. Switch anytime with /model', status line 'Chase | Fable 5.1 | ctx: --', 'auto mode on (shift+tab to cycle)'
Next Steps pane: 'What's up next, Chase?' with Overview and three option cards (commit it / polish the design / ...) after building a habit tracker
Audit result list: Rehearsal mod (demos), Project tracker, Mod doctor, Cache clock, Undo module, dictation-fix; honorable mention
Tweet (Jarrod Watts): 'I made one that connects to a multiplayer Doom server while Claude is busy...'

relevance.why: This is the biggest Claude Code platform change in the batch and Haji's core topic: mods let a solo founder bake his own guardrails (trash-instead-of-delete, backup-then-undo, cache clock, next-step pane) into the harness itself. The 'audit my last 30 sessions' prompt is a cheap way to find what to build.
